Wait, I just noticed something at line 1840-1842:

```c
i = lang_start + 2;
while (i < size && !(data[i] == *chr && data[i-1] == *chr && data[i-2] == *chr)) i++;
if (i < size) return 0;
```

This loop checks for three consecutive fence characters. But `i` starts at `lang_start + 2`. If `lang_start` is 0 (no language name), then `i = 2`. The loop checks `data[2]`, `data[1]`, `data[0]` for the fence character. This is fine.

But what if `lang_start` is `size - 1`? Then `i = size + 1`, and the while loop condition `i < size` is false, so the loop doesn't execute. Then `if (i < size)` is false, so it doesn't return 0. This is fine.

What if `lang_start` is `size - 2`? Then `i = size`, and the while loop condition `i < size` is false. Fine.

What if `lang_start` is `size - 3`? Then `i = size - 1`. The while loop checks `data[size - 1] == *chr && data[size - 2] == *chr && data[size - 3] == *chr`. All in bounds. Fine.

OK, I don't see another OOB issue in `parse_codefence`.
